````text
# #3158: CI: super run failed on a production candidate
Opened by @github-actions[bot].

[super run 41978120849](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41978120849) on #3150, the promotion of `02343deae928` into production, failed:

| Job | Result |
|---|---|
| [fuzz (3/4)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41978120849/job/127086397572) | cancelled |
| [fuzz (1/4)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41978120849/job/127086397634) | cancelled |

Each link opens that job's log. This issue stays open while the run is red and the next run that passes every job closes it. `gh workflow run super.yml --ref <branch>` runs it again on demand.

Night bot: production waits on this run, so it is yours and it comes first (`priority:high`). #3150 promotes `02343deae928`, a commit of `main`, so the fix lands on `main` like any other. Root-cause each failed job from its log and fix it in a pull request: a flake is not a root cause, so make a flaky test robust instead of re-running it, and never skip, disable or quarantine a test to get green. Reproduce it with the job's own command (CLAUDE.md, Commands; one fuzz seed is `cargo jackioh fuzz --from <seed> --seeds 1`, with `--handicap` for the handicapped wave and `--duos` for the Duos wave; a daily test is `cargo test -p <crate> <name> -- --ignored`). Say in the pull request which job here the fix makes pass and how you checked it. You cannot change `.github/`: make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere, and when the rest needs a workflow or an action, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them. Once the fix is on `main`, the next daily run there that passes promotes it, or a `/promote` on the production issue tests the newer commit sooner.

---
_Posted by `.github/workflows/super.yml`._

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `claude-7` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41988416140)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

**Goal.** I couldn't reproduce the timeout, so this plan does not root-cause it or fix it. It makes the next overrun show up in the log, with the seed named. Shards 1 and 3 of super.yml's `fuzz` job were cut off at their 90-minute `timeout-minutes`. The run as a whole was not cancelled, because `report` (`if: !cancelled()`) ran. I ran each shard's own three commands on a release `jackioh` built from `f18823b`, whose engine, cards, AI and tools sources are the same as `02343de`'s:

| Shard | Plain wave | Handicap wave | Duos wave | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 519 s | 557 s | 293 s | 22.8 min |
| 3 (`--from 5001`, Duos `--from 1001`) | 527 s | 562 s | 304 s | 23.2 min |

Every seed passed, nothing panicked, and peak memory stayed around 60 MB. The shards need about a quarter of their budget, and the 90-minute timeout itself is unchanged.

#3150 went into production 36 minutes after `02343de` was committed, so it went in by `/skip-super` and no re-run proved anything. Without the job logs, which no bot can read, the cause can't be named.

What this plan fixes is the blind spot. A fuzz wave runs its seeds under rayon and prints nothing until its last seed ends, so a stalled seed, or a runner that slows down, ends in "cancelled" with a log that names no seed. Done means every 1v1 and Duos wave in that job:
- prints its progress to stderr every minute;
- stops with a failure after 10 minutes on any one seed, naming the seed and the command that plays it alone;
- prints its slowest seed at the end.

**Files to touch.**

| Path | Kind | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/tools/src/seed_watch.rs` | new | `watched()`, `HEARTBEAT_SECS`, `SEED_STALL_BOUND_SECS`, `IN_FLIGHT_SHOWN`, `Watch`, `lock`, `longest_first`, `stall_line`, `heartbeat_line`, `keep_slowest`, `finished_line`, and `mod tests` |
| `crates/tools/src/main.rs` | change | `mod seed_watch;`; header sentence about output on stderr |
| `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs` | change | `play_seeds` goes through `watched`; new `reproduce_command`; header's clock sentence; one test in `mod fuzz_forced_cards` |
| `crates/tools/src/duos_fuzz.rs` | change | `play_duos_wave` goes through `watched`; drop `use rayon::prelude::*;` |
| `crates/tools/README.md` | change | the `fuzz` row's "Does" cell gets one sentence |

Do not touch `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `.claude/`, any pure crate (`crates/engine`, `cards`, `ai`, `luau`, `run`, `shared`), `spec/` or `scripts/`. No rules decision is made, so there is no ruling. The determinism rules that apply are §9.3 and §10.7, and CLAUDE.md rule 4. They are kept because only `crates/tools` reads the clock, and never inside a game.

**Steps.**

1. **New file `crates/tools/src/seed_watch.rs`.**
   - Header `//!`: "The fuzz waves' watch (#3158). A wave's seeds run under rayon and its summary prints only once the last one ends, so super.yml's `fuzz` job, cut off at 90 minutes, left a log naming no seed. `watched` prints to stderr, every `HEARTBEAT_SECS`, how many seeds are done and which have run longest. When one seed has run past `SEED_STALL_BOUND_SECS`, it prints that seed and the command that plays it alone, then ends the process with exit code 1. After the wave it prints the slowest seed. Only the wall clock is read, and never by a game."
   - Constants:
     - `pub const HEARTBEAT_SECS: u64 = 60;`
     - `pub const SEED_STALL_BOUND_SECS: u64 = 600;`. Its doc comment gives the slowest seed you measure in step 6 (the waves' `slowest:` lines) and the planner's shard times above.
     - `pub const IN_FLIGHT_SHOWN: usize = 3;`
   - Code. Copy this, keeping the names:

```rust
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU32, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Mutex, MutexGuard, PoisonError, mpsc};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
use indexmap::IndexMap;
use rayon::prelude::*;

#[derive(Default)]
struct Watch {
    running: Mutex<IndexMap<u32, Instant>>,
    done: AtomicU32,
    slowest: Mutex<Option<(u32, Duration)>>,
}

fn lock<T>(mutex: &Mutex<T>) -> MutexGuard<'_, T> {
    mutex.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
}

/// `run` over seeds `from..from + ran` under rayon, results in seed order, watched as the header says.
pub(crate) fn watched<T: Send>(
    label: &str,
    from: u32,
    ran: u32,
    reproduce: impl Fn(u32) -> String + Sync,
    run: impl Fn(u32) -> T + Sync + Send,
) -> Vec<T> {
    let watch = Watch::default();
    let shared = &watch;
    let reproduce = &reproduce;
    let started = Instant::now();
    let (stop, stopped) = mpsc::channel::<()>();
    let results = std::thread::scope(|scope| {
        scope.spawn(move || {
            while let Err(mpsc::RecvTimeoutError::Timeout) =
                stopped.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(HEARTBEAT_SECS))
            {
                let now = Instant::now();
                let ages: Vec<(u32, Duration)> = lock(&shared.running)
                    .iter()
                    .map(|(seed, began)| (*seed, now.duration_since(*began)))
                    .collect();
                let bound = Duration::from_secs(SEED_STALL_BOUND_SECS);
                if let Some(line) = stall_line(label, &ages, bound, reproduce) {
                    eprintln!("{line}");
                    std::process::exit(1);
                }
                let done = shared.done.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
                eprintln!("{}", heartbeat_line(label, done, ran, started.elapsed(), &ages));
            }
        });
        let results: Vec<T> = (from..from + ran)
            .into_par_iter()
            .map(|seed| {
                let began = Instant::now();
                lock(&shared.running).insert(seed, began);
                let result = run(seed);
                lock(&shared.running).swap_remove(&seed);
                shared.done.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
                keep_slowest(&mut lock(&shared.slowest), seed, began.elapsed());
                result
            })
            .collect();
        drop(stop);
        results
    });
    eprintln!("{}", finished_line(label, ran, started.elapsed(), *lock(&watch.slowest)));
    results
}
```

   - Helper functions, each with a doc comment:
     - `fn longest_first(ages: &[(u32, Duration)]) -> Vec<(u32, Duration)>`: a copy sorted by age, longest first; on a tie the lower seed comes first.
     - `fn stall_line(label: &str, ages: &[(u32, Duration)], bound: Duration, reproduce: &dyn Fn(u32) -> String) -> Option<String>`: looks only at the first entry of `longest_first`. It returns `None` unless that age is strictly greater than `bound`. Otherwise it returns:
       `format!("[{label}] seed {seed} has run {}s, past SEED_STALL_BOUND_SECS ({}s): it stalled, so the wave stops here, failing\n  reproduce: {}", age.as_secs(), bound.as_secs(), reproduce(seed))`
     - `fn heartbeat_line(label: &str, done: u32, ran: u32, elapsed: Duration, ages: &[(u32, Duration)]) -> String` returns:
       `"[{label}] {done} of {ran} seeds done in {elapsed_secs}s; running longest: {list}"`
       `{list}` is the first `IN_FLIGHT_SHOWN` entries of `longest_first`, each written `seed {seed} ({secs}s)` and joined by `", "`. It is `none` when no seed is running.
     - `fn keep_slowest(slowest: &mut Option<(u32, Duration)>, seed: u32, took: Duration)`: replaces the kept value when there is none, when `took` is longer, or when `took` is equal and `seed` is lower.
     - `fn finished_line(label: &str, ran: u32, elapsed: Duration, slowest: Option<(u32, Duration)>) -> String` returns:
       `"[{label}] {ran} seeds in {secs}s; slowest: seed {seed}, {ms}ms"`, or `slowest: none` when there is no seed.

2. **`crates/tools/src/main.rs`.**
   - Add `mod seed_watch;` between `mod sample_size;` and `mod selfplay;`.
   - In the header, change "Output goes to stdout;" to "Output goes to stdout (a fuzz wave's progress lines go to stderr, `seed_watch.rs`);".

3. **`crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs`.**
   - (a) In `play_seeds`, replace `let results: Vec<Result<Passed, Failure>> = (from..from + ran).into_par_iter().map(seed).collect();` with:
     `crate::seed_watch::watched(wave_name(handicapped), from, ran, |at| reproduce_command(at, handicapped, forcing), seed)`
     Keep the same `let results: Vec<Result<Passed, Failure>> =` binding. Leave `started_at` and `elapsed_ms` as they are.
   - (b) Add this beside `wave_name`, and leave the report's own `reproduce:` line alone:

```rust
/// The command that plays `seed` of this wave alone, as a stalled seed's report gives it (#3158).
fn reproduce_command(seed: u32, handicapped: bool, forcing: &Forcing) -> String {
    format!(
        "cargo jackioh fuzz --from {seed} --seeds 1{}{}",
        if handicapped { " --handicap" } else { "" },
        if forcing.named.is_empty() { String::new() } else { format!(" --cards {}", forcing.named.join(",")) }
    )
}
```

   - (c) In the header, change "(the clock only times the wave)" to "(the clock only times the wave and watches it for a stalled seed, `seed_watch.rs`, #3158)".
   - Keep `use rayon::prelude::*;` in this file: `regress` still uses `par_iter`.

4. **`crates/tools/src/duos_fuzz.rs`.**
   - Change the body of `play_duos_wave` to:
     `register_all(); crate::seed_watch::watched("fuzz-duos", from, ran, |seed| format!("cargo jackioh fuzz --duos --from {seed} --seeds 1"), fuzz_duos_seed)`
   - Delete `use rayon::prelude::*;` (line 36). Nothing else in the file uses it, and clippy `-D warnings` fails on an unused import.

5. **`crates/tools/README.md`.** In the `fuzz` row's "Does" cell only (the acceptance test reads the first cell), append:
   "While a wave or the Duos wave runs, `seed_watch.rs` prints to stderr every `HEARTBEAT_SECS` the seeds done and the `IN_FLIGHT_SHOWN` running longest, and after it the slowest seed. A seed running past `SEED_STALL_BOUND_SECS` stops the run with exit code 1, naming the seed and its `--from N --seeds 1` command, so a stall fails inside super.yml's 90 minutes instead of being cancelled with no seed named (#3158)."

6. **Measure.**
   - Build: `cargo build --release -p jackioh-tools`. The binary lands in `$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/release/jackioh` when that variable is set.
   - Run shard 1's three commands from any directory:
     - `jackioh fuzz --from 1 --seeds 2500`
     - `jackioh fuzz --from 1 --seeds 2500 --handicap`
     - `jackioh fuzz --duos --from 1 --seeds 500`
   - Write each wall time and each `slowest:` line into the `SEED_STALL_BOUND_SECS` doc comment.
   - If any seed takes more than 60 s, stop and report it: the bound would then be too tight to stand.

**Tests.** The new tests go in `crates/tools/src/seed_watch.rs` under `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`:
- `a_watched_wave_returns_every_result_in_seed_order`: `watched("test", 5, 40, |s| format!("again {s}"), |s| s * 3)` equals `(5..45).map(|s| s * 3).collect::<Vec<u32>>()`. It also does the same inside `rayon::ThreadPoolBuilder::new().num_threads(1).build().unwrap().install(..)`.
- `a_seed_past_the_bound_is_named_with_its_command`: ages `[(3, 5 s), (812, 601 s), (9, 700 s)]`, bound 600 s, and reproduce `|s| format!("cargo jackioh fuzz --from {s} --seeds 1")`. The line contains `seed 9 has run 700s`, `SEED_STALL_BOUND_SECS (600s)` and `reproduce: cargo jackioh fuzz --from 9 --seeds 1`.
- `no_seed_at_or_under_the_bound_is_a_stall`: `[(1, 600 s)]` with bound 600 s gives `None`, and `[]` gives `None`.
- `a_heartbeat_counts_the_done_seeds_and_names_the_longest_running`: label `w`, done 1200, ran 2500, elapsed 300 s, ages `[(1,1s),(2,9s),(3,4s),(4,9s)]`. The result equals `[w] 1200 of 2500 seeds done in 300s; running longest: seed 2 (9s), seed 4 (9s), seed 3 (4s)`. With no ages it ends in `running longest: none`.
- `the_slowest_seed_is_kept_and_a_tie_keeps_the_lower_seed`: covers `keep_slowest` and `finished_line` (`slowest: seed 7, 1500ms`, and `slowest: none`).

The new test in `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs`, under `mod fuzz_forced_cards`:
- `a_stalled_seeds_command_names_its_wave_and_forced_cards`:
  - `reproduce_command(12, false, &Forcing::default())` equals `cargo jackioh fuzz --from 12 --seeds 1`.
  - With `true` it ends in ` --handicap`.
  - With `&forcing_of(&["core-t-felinor"]).unwrap()` it ends in ` --cards core-t-felinor`.

Commands:
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools seed_watch`
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --features jackioh-engine/testkit fuzz` (the whole fuzz suite, including the Duos and thread-count tests)
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test acceptance readme`

**Done when.**
- [ ] Steps 1–5 are in, and `watched` is the only path for the 1v1 and Duos waves.
- [ ] The tests above pass.
- [ ] Shard 1's three commands pass on the new release binary, timed, and their stderr shows heartbeat lines and the `slowest:` lines.
- [ ] `jackioh fuzz --seeds 200` (CI's gate) passes with stdout unchanged in shape. Heartbeats go to stderr only.
- [ ] The harness's checks pass: rustfmt, catalog, patches, rulings, clippy, cargo tests and web tests. `rulings` should be untouched, since nothing cites an R-id.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` reports no card change. This is a tools-only, Internal change, so no pending fragment is needed.
- [ ] The PR body says:
  - Which jobs: `fuzz (1/4)` and `fuzz (3/4)`.
  - Their own commands pass locally: the planner's times above plus yours. Nothing in a seed's play changed.
  - The timeout did not reproduce, so the PR makes a future overrun name its seed and fail within minutes. It does not claim a root cause.
  - It points to the person's step under Open questions.
  - Each decision below, with the alternative rejected.

Decisions, with the rejected alternatives:
- The watch is a thread beside rayon, rather than a per-seed check inside `play_game`: a hung seed never returns to a check of its own.
- A stall calls `exit(1)` rather than only printing: that fails the job with the seed named, where printing alone leaves it "cancelled" at 90 minutes.
- The bound is 600 s, rather than something near the slowest seed: wall time on a loaded runner must never fail a healthy seed. The 5 s `CHECKPOINT_TIME_BOUND_MS` was already loosened once for that reason (#1803).
- `--regress` is not watched: super.yml's `fuzz` job doesn't run it.

**Risks.**
- **Determinism.** The watch reads only `Instant`, and only in `crates/tools`. Seeds, streams, results and their order (`collect` keeps it) don't change, so replay, hashes and the summary stay byte for byte the same. `the_coverage_is_the_same_on_one_thread_and_on_four` must still pass.
- **Flakes.** The 600 s bound is far above any seed here (a whole 2,500-seed wave is about 520 s on 4 cores). Step 6 records the real slowest seed.
- **Output contract.** `--json` and the summary stay on stdout, and only stderr gains lines. Nothing in the repository parses the fuzz's stderr. I checked with grep in `scripts/`, `bot/go`, `e2e/` and `crates/tools/tests`.
- **Locks.** The mutexes are never held while a seed runs, and poisoning is ignored (`lock`).
- **`exit(1)` skips destructors.** Nothing is lost: stdout's summary isn't printed yet, and stderr is unbuffered.
- **Purity.** No pure crate changes, so CLAUDE.md rule 4 isn't touched.

**Open questions.**
- **A person must read the two job logs, which no bot can open:** [fuzz (1/4)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41978120849/job/127086397634) and [fuzz (3/4)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41978120849/job/127086397572). Note which step was running when the 90 minutes ran out and the last line it printed. What to do next depends on where it stopped:
  - **In `actions/download-artifact` or `checkout`:** the fix is a step bound in `.github/workflows/super.yml`'s `fuzz` job, which only a person can change. Add `timeout-minutes: 10` under `- uses: actions/download-artifact@v4`, at the same indent as its `with:`.
  - **In "this quarter's seeds" or "this quarter's Duos seeds", with a wave summary already printed:** this PR's next run will name the stalled seed.
  - **In those steps, with no summary printed:** the binary was running slowly or was stuck. The heartbeat lines this PR adds will show which.
  - Also check the fuzz shard times of the daily super run on `main` from 2026-11-05 07:17 UTC. They should be about 25 minutes.
- The difficulty rule would rate this item medium: tools only, five files. The `hard` label set by a person stands.
````
